headline: OpenSSH bypass draws immediate exploit attempts as Barracuda patches a root chain
standfirst: Attempted exploitation of an OpenSSH authentication bypass began within hours of disclosure, with one honeypot rooted, while QNAP and WordPress users face live attacks and Barracuda patches an unauthenticated root chain.
bodyMarkdown:
## Actively exploited

Threat actors began attempting to exploit CVE-2026-123158, an OpenSSH authentication bypass nicknamed SSHole, within hours of disclosure, and one honeypot was rooted, according to [[s8]]. The High-severity flaw (CVSS 8.1) affects Linux systems running OpenSSH on musl libc without PAM; NVD says some account configurations accept any password between 256 and 1,024 characters, and the excerpt notes sign-ins to accounts with no password set. Analysis: the narrow configuration still leaves exposed musl-based servers the story to watch.

QNAP says hackers are exploiting the Plex2Shell vulnerability chain against NAS devices and urges users to update Plex Media Server to the latest version in the QNAP App Center [[s4]]. The supplied excerpt gives no CVE, affected versions or post-exploitation detail, so exposed appliances remain the immediate concern.

Sites running an actively exploited WordPress flaw can be exposed again while installing the fix, because the update unpacks files using the site's old, unpatched code; an attacker who strikes at the right moment can run code on the server [[s6]]. Analysis: the patch window itself becomes part of the incident response.

## Breaches

Chainalysis says an attack on its systems and internal tools exposed credentials and live tokens for all customers [[s13]]. Analysis: that makes it a customer-wide credential problem, not just a vendor incident.

## Vulnerabilities

Barracuda's Email Security Gateway has two flaws that researchers chained to run commands as root with no login; patches are available and the chain has been detailed publicly [[s31]]. The named flaw, CVE-2026-116606, is Critical (CVSS 9.3) in versions earlier than 9.4.0.030: an unauthenticated remote attacker can invoke a configuration-import function and restore a crafted backup archive, modifying the appliance's global configuration. The second flaw and the chain's full prerequisites were not supplied.

D-Link has published mitigation measures for multiple unpatched zero-days in DGS-3130 series managed switches, with no patches supplied in the excerpt [[s19]]. Analysis: for those models, mitigation is the only near-term defense.

## Industry

The FBI and CISA warn that hackers are actively targeting industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems worldwide, with potential food spoilage, equipment damage and fire hazards [[s33]]. Analysis: that puts physical safety and supply-chain continuity, not just data confidentiality, in the threat model.

## Research

APT29, described as Russian state-sponsored, is compromising websites, fingerprinting visitors and harvesting information from the interesting ones, in a campaign targeting thousands of mobile users [[s42]]. Analysis: the mobile focus suggests watering-hole tradecraft tuned to a different endpoint.

selected.excerpt: Threat actors are attempting to exploit a recently disclosed security flaw impacting OpenSSH that can enable sign-ins to accounts that have no password set, according to Previdian. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-123158 (CVSS score: 8.1) and codenamed SSHole (or *sshole), impacts Linux systems that run OpenSSH on the musl C library with Pluggable Authentication Modules (PAM) disabled,

nvd.description: sshd in OpenSSH before 10.6p2 on Linux, when musl libc is used without PAM, lacks a workaround for a password authentication bypass (related to misinterpretation of whether a string is intended to be a password hash). For some configurations of accounts, any password between 256 and 1024 characters succeeds. An example of a platform using musl libc without PAM is Alpine Linux.

selected.angle: Attempted exploitation began within hours of disclosure and one honeypot was rooted, showing the OpenSSH SSHole auth bypass is an immediate threat to exposed musl-based servers.
